title: Moral relativism and truth
tagline: Answer "that is true for you" and show why truth, conscience and natural law matter.
whyItMatters: Most people your age or older live with a quiet relativism: "who am I to judge?". It makes moral conversation hard and can excuse real harm.

mindset.tip: Start with what the person cares about (fairness, kindness, tolerance) and show that these already assume real moral truth.
Ask questions: "Is it wrong to be intolerant? Would it be wrong if everyone agreed it was fine?".
Distinguish humility about what we know from denial that anything can be known.
Respect conscience, even a wrongly formed one; we persuade, we do not force (CCC 1782, 1790-1794; Dignitatis Humanae 1-3).

resources.title: Defeating the "Dictatorship of Relativism"
resources.creator: Trent Horn (Counsel of Trent)
resources.why: Shows why relativism contradicts itself and how to answer it kindly.

resources.title: Letter from a Birmingham Jail
resources.creator: Martin Luther King Jr.
resources.why: A famous case that unjust laws can be judged by a standard higher than law.
resources.note: Baptist minister; text hosted by the University of Pennsylvania

resources.title: How to Refute Moral Relativism
resources.creator: Karlo Broussard
resources.why: Explains why living as a relativist breaks down in practice.

resources.title: Who's Intolerant: the Relativist or the Absolutist?
resources.creator: Karlo Broussard
resources.why: Answers the claim that believing in absolutes means being intolerant.

resources.title: Argument from Conscience
resources.creator: Peter Kreeft
resources.why: Starts from the sense of right and wrong that nearly everyone has.
resources.note: Catholic philosopher; free on his own site

resources.title: Five Fatal Flaws of Moral Relativism
resources.creator: Greg Koukl (Stand to Reason)
resources.why: Practical questions to ask someone who says morality is just opinion.
resources.note: By a Protestant apologist; used here for the argument only

resources.title: A Refutation of Moral Relativism (audio lecture and transcript)
resources.creator: Peter Kreeft
resources.why: A lecture that answers the usual reasons people give for relativism, with a written transcript.
resources.note: Catholic philosopher; audio quality is plain

resources.title: Letter to the Duke of Norfolk, Section 5: Conscience and the Pope
resources.creator: John Henry Newman
resources.why: Newman's well-known account of conscience as a messenger, not a mere feeling.
resources.note: Public-domain text on the Newman Reader

resources.title: Dignitatis Humanae (Declaration on Religious Freedom)
resources.creator: Second Vatican Council
resources.why: The Church's case that conscience must be free precisely because truth matters.

resources.title: Gaudium et Spes (Pastoral Constitution on the Church in the Modern World)
resources.creator: Second Vatican Council
resources.why: Paragraphs 19-22 describe atheism, its causes, and how the Church should answer.

resources.title: Evangelium Vitae (The Gospel of Life)
resources.creator: Pope St. John Paul II
resources.why: Paragraphs 19-20 and 69-70 show how relativism affects law and life.

resources.title: Veritatis Splendor (The Splendor of Truth)
resources.creator: Pope St. John Paul II
resources.why: The Church's main teaching on moral truth, conscience and objective good and evil.

resources.title: Summa Theologiae I-II, Question 94: The natural law
resources.creator: Thomas Aquinas
resources.why: The classic account of the natural law, in Aquinas's own words.

resources.title: Moral Relativism
resources.creator: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
resources.why: The best philosophical case for relativism, fairly stated.
resources.note: Secular scholarly reference; the other side in its strongest form

resources.title: Natural Law Theories
resources.creator: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
resources.why: A neutral overview of natural law, including its secular forms.

resources.title: Theaetetus (Plato's reply to Protagoras)
resources.creator: Plato
